record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Multiple susceptible compartments in SIR-PH-type epidemic models
record.original_question: How can the endemic-equilibrium and stability theory for SIR-PH-type epidemic models be extended to models with two or more susceptible compartments that can become infected, such as SEIT-type models?

evidence.quote:
Study the case of two or more compartments susceptible to become infected (for example the SEIT
model [51, 39]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a deterministic compartmental epidemic model of SIR-PH type, defined as follows. The population is split into:
- a susceptible compartment S,
- a vector x = (x_1, ..., x_n) of "disease" compartments (e.g., exposed, infected of various types, treated), whose dynamics, while individuals are infectious, are governed by a phase-type law with sub-generator matrix A ∈ R^{n×n} and initial-distribution row vector α (with α·1 = 1), so that the force of infection is β S (α·x) for some transmission rate β > 0,
- a removed/recovered compartment R, with loss of immunity at rate γ_R ≥ 0 feeding back into S,
together with a constant linear birth rate Λ > 0 into S, a natural death rate μ > 0 in every compartment, an additional disease-induced mortality vector δ ≥ 0 acting on x, and possibly a vaccination flow from S to R at rate ν ≥ 0 with vaccination-fatality rate δ_v ≥ 0. The full ODE system is

  S' = Λ − μ S − β S (α·x) + γ_R R − ν S,
  x' = β S (α·x) e_α + A^⊤ x − diag(δ) x,    (here e_α represents the entry distribution α)
  R' = (−A·1 − δ − μ)·x · (something) + ν S − (μ + γ_R + δ_v) R,

with the basic reproduction number R_0 = β α (−A)^{−1} 1 · (Λ/(μ+ν)).

For this class one has a complete theory: a disease-free equilibrium that is globally asymptotically stable when R_0 ≤ 1, and a unique endemic equilibrium that is (locally, and under standard hypotheses globally) asymptotically stable when R_0 > 1.

Problem. Extend this endemic-equilibrium existence/uniqueness theory and the associated local and global stability analysis to SIR-PH-type models in which the single susceptible compartment S is replaced by two or more distinct susceptible compartments S_1, ..., S_k (k ≥ 2), each of which can become infected (possibly with different transmission rates β_i, different demographic parameters, and inter-compartment transition rates). In particular, formulate the appropriate next-generation-matrix definition of R_0, prove the existence and uniqueness of the endemic equilibrium when R_0 > 1, and establish global asymptotic stability results paralleling the single-S case. The motivating example is the SEIT-type model with both a "susceptible" and a "treated-but-susceptible-again" compartment that can each be infected.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific follow-up work was located that explicitly extends the full SIR-PH endemic-equilibrium and global-stability framework to the case of multiple susceptible compartments (such as SEIT-type models). Partial results exist in the broader literature on multi-group/multi-susceptible SIR and SEIT models, but a unified SIR-PH treatment matching the single-S case appears not to be available, so the status is treated as unknown.
